title: A smooth curve function field has a singleton p-basis
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-pc-field-characteristic], where $p$ is prime. Let $C$ be a smooth integral $k$-curve of dimension one [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], and put $K=k(C)$ [def-sc-function-field], with its given inclusion $k\hookrightarrow K$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Write $K^p=\{x^p:x\in K\}$, a subfield of $K$, and let $(\Omega_{K/k},\mathrm d)$ be its module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $k\subseteq K^p$, $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=1$, and there is $t\in K$ such that $(\mathrm dt)$ is a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/k}$ and $(1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1})$, indexed by $0\leq j<p$, is a $K^p$-basis of $K$. In particular $[K:K^p]=p$ [def-pc-field-tower]. Properness is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (curves-lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), proof, second paragraph, the dimension-one differential and p-basis calculation; more-algebra.tex Tag 07P2 (more-algebra-lemma-p-basis), existence and equivalence (a)-(b).

proof.text: For every $a\in k$, the nonconstant polynomial $X^p-a$ has a root $b\in k$ by algebraic closedness, so $a=b^p$ also in $K$. Thus $k\subseteq K^p$ and the compositum $kK^p$ equals $K^p$. Here $K^p$ is a subfield: in characteristic $p$ one has $x^p+y^p=(x+y)^p$, $x^py^p=(xy)^p$, $-x^p=(-x)^p$, and $(x^p)^{-1}=(x^{-1})^p$ for $x\ne0$.

source.place: Tags 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and 07P2 (lemma-p-basis): coefficient subfield kK^p; specialization to algebraically closed k.

proof.text: The curve $C$ is a separated integral $k$-scheme of finite type of dimension one, smooth over $k$, i.e. a smooth curve over the field $k$ in the sense of [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-generic-differentials]; its generic point $\eta$ gives $K=k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ with the $k$-algebra structure of the structure morphism, which is the given inclusion $k\hookrightarrow K$. The last clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-generic-differentials] says that $\Omega_{K/k}$ is nonzero of dimension one over $K$. Choose $v\ne0$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$; then $(v)$ is a $K$-basis and $\dim_K\Omega_{K/k}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), proof, second paragraph: 'Since X is a smooth curve we know that Omega_{K/k} is a vector space of dimension 1 over K'.

proof.text: The empty family in $K$ is $p$-independent over $k$: its sole bounded monomial is $1$, which is linearly independent over the field $kK^p=K^p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-p-independent-extends-to-p-basis] to this family, obtaining $(t_i)_{i\in I}$ whose bounded finitely supported monomials form a $K^p$-basis of $K$. The characteristic of $K$ is $p$ because $k\hookrightarrow K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis] to the extension $K/k$ and this monomial basis. It gives a $K$-basis $(\mathrm dt_i)_{i\in I}$ of $\Omega_{K/k}$.

source.place: Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), existence by extending the empty p-independent family and implication (a) implies (b).

proof.text: The index set $I$ is nonempty, since otherwise the span of $(\mathrm dt_i)$ would be zero, contradicting $v\ne0$. Choose $i_0\in I$. In the basis $(v)$ write $\mathrm dt_i=a_i v$; every $a_i$ is nonzero since a basis vector is nonzero. If $j\ne i_0$, the equality $a_j\mathrm dt_{i_0}-a_{i_0}\mathrm dt_j=0$ is a relation in the basis $(\mathrm dt_i)$ with nonzero coefficients, a contradiction. Thus $I=\{i_0\}$, and for $t=t_{i_0}$ the vector $\mathrm dt$ alone is a $K$-basis.

source.place: Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), elementary dimension-one consequence of (a) implies (b); curves.tex Tag 0CCY, second paragraph of proof.

proof.text: For the singleton index set $I=\{i_0\}$, a bounded exponent family $E$ is specified uniquely by $j=E(i_0)$, with $0\le j<p$, and its monomial is $t^j$. Reindex the monomial basis from step 3 by these integers. It is exactly $(1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1})$, so $K$ has dimension $p$ over $K^p$. By the definition of field degree [def-pc-field-tower] this says $[K:K^p]=p$. None of the preceding steps used properness.

source.place: Tags 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), bounded monomial basis for a singleton; curves.tex Tag 0CCY, second paragraph, degree calculation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q102-28d9a7b11 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full. It has six steps and no new nodes, and its statement is unchanged; I also read Stacks 0CCY (proof, second paragraph) and 07P1/07P2. The statement is true: it needs k algebraically closed so that kK^p=K^p (k=F_p(s), K=k(u) is a counterexample otherwise), and it does not need properness. Small cases A^1 and G_m give t=u, and for p=2 the basis is 1,u. Step checks: step 1 (X^p-a, including a=0, and K^p is a subfield) is correct. Steps 2-3 (dim_eta C=1, 02G1 rank-one affine W, localization at A minus 0) are correct as written. Step 4 starts from the empty family, which is p-independent; the extension node gives a monomial K^p-basis and the 07P2 (a)=>(b) node gives the differential basis. I checked both nodes' hypotheses, characteristic p and coefficient field kK^p. Step 5: if the index set had two elements i0, j, then a_j dt_{i0} - a_{i0} dt_j = 0 would be a nontrivial relation, so it is a singleton. Step 6 reindexes the basis to 1,...,t^{p-1} and gets [K:K^p]=p. Fault (C5/C7): steps 2-3 re-derive dim_K Omega_{K/k}=1 through tools of other units (sk-prop-jacobian, and sk-thm-p1 for 02G1/00RT). The item's own unit already has the split, reviewed node lem-sfb-smooth-curve-generic-differentials, which is on base and does not depend on the item; it states exactly that Omega_{F/k} is nonzero of dimension one for a smooth curve over a field, which is the 0CCY sentence the item realizes.
